description: Fields from competitors/findings.jsonl that the contract has no place for, keyed by contract record_id / claim_id. Not read by the team validator or exporter.

luis:eu_challengers-F0093.statement: Forum user states after a one-hour test drive that build quality and materials are high, and the interior beats his own Mercedes C-Class and is far ahead of a VW ID.3.

luis:eu_challengers-F0094.statement: Forum user states after a test drive that performance and chassis are at least at Mercedes level.

luis:eu_challengers-F0095.statement: Forum user states after a test drive that the controls are easy to use.

luis:eu_challengers-F0096.statement: Forum user states after a test drive that lane keeping worked fairly well.

luis:eu_challengers-F0097.statement: Forum user states after a test drive that the cameras are high resolution.

luis:eu_challengers-F0098.statement: Forum user likes that the tow hitch extends on its own and is rated for 2 tonnes.

luis:eu_challengers-F0099.statement: Forum user criticises that the rear bench does not fold down.

luis:eu_challengers-F0100.statement: Forum user criticises the small tailgate opening.

luis:eu_challengers-F0101.statement: Forum user calls the NOMI dashboard robot head a nice gimmick.

luis:eu_challengers-F0102.statement: Forum user states after a one-hour test drive that materials and finish are good.

luis:eu_challengers-F0103.statement: Forum user found consumption of about 24 kWh/100 km at 130 km/h in Eco at 10 degrees C acceptable.

luis:eu_challengers-F0104.statement: Forum user states the suspension is too soft in Eco and Normal, making it hard to hold a clean line on winding roads, while Sport modes are much better.

luis:eu_challengers-F0105.statement: Forum user finds power in Eco and Normal modes too weak, while Sport modes accelerate strongly.

luis:eu_challengers-F0106.statement: Forum user states NOMI only understood him in a quiet cabin, not while the radio was playing.

luis:eu_challengers-F0107.statement: Forum user wants a dedicated voice-control button.

luis:eu_challengers-F0108.statement: Forum user states the lane assist corrects constantly, making the steering wheel jitter.

luis:eu_challengers-F0109.statement: Forum user finds the boot small and impractical for a 5 m car, with no compartment for charging cables.

luis:eu_challengers-F0110.statement: Forum user criticises that there is no frunk.

luis:eu_challengers-F0111.statement: Forum user states the radio was offline most of the test drive, with no apparent internet connection.

luis:eu_challengers-F0112.statement: Forum user states the dealer staff were inexperienced with modern electric cars.

luis:eu_challengers-F0182.statement: Forum user who test-drove both cars and ordered the Tesla prefers its larger boot over the BYD Seal's.

luis:eu_challengers-F0183.statement: Forum user prefers the Tesla's larger frunk over the BYD Seal's.

luis:eu_challengers-F0184.statement: Forum user values that the Tesla has roof-load and towing ratings, which the BYD Seal lacks.

luis:eu_challengers-F0185.statement: Forum user chose the Tesla over the BYD Seal mainly for its lower consumption.

luis:eu_challengers-F0186.statement: Forum user values the Tesla's faster charging according to tests.

luis:eu_challengers-F0187.statement: Forum user values the Supercharger network.

luis:eu_challengers-F0188.statement: Forum user likes the rear touchscreen for the children.

luis:eu_challengers-F0189.statement: Forum user likes that the Tesla has no mandatory service intervals.

luis:eu_challengers-F0190.statement: Forum user dislikes the missing indicator stalk.

luis:eu_challengers-F0191.statement: Forum user dislikes the missing wiper stalk.

luis:eu_challengers-F0192.statement: Forum user misses ultrasonic parking sensors.

luis:eu_challengers-F0193.statement: Forum user sees the ambient lighting as a gimmick.

luis:eu_challengers-F0194.statement: Forum user (2020 Model 3 owner) states after a test drive of the new Model 3 Performance that the chassis is now on par with German makers.

luis:eu_challengers-F0195.statement: Forum user states after a test drive that the noise level is now on par with German makers.

luis:eu_challengers-F0196.statement: Forum user states tyre rolling noise at higher speeds is louder than in his older Model 3.

luis:eu_challengers-F0197.statement: Forum user praises the seat ventilation.

luis:eu_challengers-F0198.statement: Forum user finds the seats good overall.

luis:eu_challengers-F0199.statement: Forum user found the acceleration of the new Model 3 Performance impressive.

luis:eu_challengers-F0200.statement: Forum user states gear selection on the display worked without problems.

luis:eu_challengers-F0201.statement: Forum user found the indicator buttons very unusual and missed the signal at the first five roundabouts.

luis:eu_challengers-F0202.statement: Forum user states fan noise is audible when the audio is off.

luis:eu_challengers-F0203.statement: Forum user states the headrest sits further forward than in his 2020 car.

luis:eu_challengers-F0204.statement: Forum user states the brakes need high pedal force and bite less than expected.

luis:eu_challengers-F0205.statement: Forum user dislikes that the speed-warning beep must be disabled before every trip.

luis:eu_challengers-F0206.statement: Forum user wants a towbar; with the indicator buttons, its absence made the car not right for him yet.

luis:eu_challengers-F0207.statement: Forum user (2020 Model 3 owner) states after test-driving the new SR and Performance that he wants the ventilated seats.

luis:eu_challengers-F0208.statement: Forum user states the indicator button operation annoys him.

luis:eu_challengers-F0209.statement: Owner of a Model 3 Highland RWD Long Range reports about 722 km from a full charge with 43 km left, including Autopilot and up to 140 km/h, and says daily driving beats the displayed range.

luis:eu_challengers-F0210.statement: Owner likes the always-online browser for entertainment.

luis:eu_german-F0123.statement: Owner (company car, new since November 2024) states they are very happy with the EQE and finds much of the online criticism unfounded.

luis:eu_german-F0124.statement: Owner states the rear-wheel steering makes the car very manoeuvrable and recommends ordering it.

luis:eu_german-F0125.statement: Owner (EQE 300, built 11/2023) calls the front camera valuable because the view ahead over the bonnet is almost nil, and says the rear camera works well.

luis:eu_german-F0126.statement: Owner states the 360-degree camera greys out exactly the area closest to the car, which would be the most useful.

luis:eu_german-F0127.statement: Owner states they use the traffic-light camera view daily.

luis:eu_german-F0128.statement: Owner states the optional Burmester sound system is better than the standard one.

luis:eu_german-F0129.statement: Owner states the Digital Light projector headlights are worth having.

luis:eu_german-F0130.statement: Owner states the standard comfort suspension is excellent and air suspension is not needed.

luis:eu_german-F0131.statement: Owner states the boot is smaller than expected: a golf bag requires folding a rear seat section, and two golf bags the whole bench.

luis:eu_german-F0132.statement: Owner wishes they had 22 kW AC charging; their car has 11 kW because 22 kW was an extra-cost option.

luis:eu_german-F0133.statement: Owner wishes for front seat ventilation.

luis:eu_german-F0134.statement: Owner notes the upholstery is faux leather and wishes for genuine leather.

luis:eu_german-F0135.statement: Owner says they love the car and find the design beautiful despite online criticism.

luis:eu_german-F0136.statement: Owner (EQE 300, about one month and 3,500 km) reports more interior creaks and rattles than expected for Mercedes' quality standard, otherwise no failures.

luis:eu_german-F0137.statement: Owner finds acceleration good up to 120 km/h but sluggish above that despite 245 PS, attributing it to the S-Class-like weight.

luis:eu_german-F0138.vfc_level2: Drive, driving dynamics and chassis, overall technology
luis:eu_german-F0138.statement: Forum user describing an EQE 300 (ownership not stated) praises a comfortable yet precise chassis well suited to long motorway trips.

luis:eu_german-F0139.statement: Forum user states the EQE has noticeably more interior space than the EQA or EQB.

luis:eu_german-F0140.statement: Forum user states charging power could be higher: the 400-volt architecture is mature and reliable but not fast.

luis:eu_german-F0141.statement: Owner (EQE 350+, bought used with 5,000 km, four weeks of ownership, switched from an Ioniq 5) describes the ride as like a flying carpet and does not regret the switch.

luis:eu_german-F0244.statement: Owner (A6 Avant e-tron quattro, experienced BEV driver) reports real motorway range above 450 km, doing two non-stop 404 km legs mostly at about 150 km/h on about 22.4 kWh/100 km.

luis:eu_german-F0245.statement: Owner reports charging 54.9 kWh from 9 % to 63 % in 13 minutes at an IONITY charger, briefly seeing 280 kW, with a charging curve better than expected.

luis:eu_german-F0246.statement: Owner rates the driver assistance as the best on the market: adaptive cruise, lane keeping and sign-based speed adaptation work well, with timely braking for limits and smooth acceleration.

luis:eu_german-F0247.statement: Owner names the missing overtaking (automatic lane-change) assistant as the only limitation of the assistance system.

luis:eu_german-F0248.statement: Owner finds the sign-based speed control often too slow for their taste.

luis:eu_german-F0249.statement: Same owner reports over 340 km of range in winter below -5 degrees C at average speeds above 120 km/h.

luis:eu_german-F0250.vfc_level2: Driver assistance, automated driving, overall technology
luis:eu_german-F0250.statement: Forum user who drove an A6 e-tron (not owned) enjoyed it and considers Audi's assistance systems a current reference, worth paying extra for on the motorway.

luis:eu_german-F0251.statement: Forum user who drove two A6 e-tron workshop loan cars says Audi is no longer premium except in its prices.
